notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, CL2; never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null); no hardware or real MuJoCo run is claimed and the fake was not compared with an upstream run. The fake is an analytic stand-in for the GymEnv wrapper: it models reset option validation, one episode sample, a reduced qpos observation (arm 7 joints, gripper 2 joints), action dict application, the 500-step task horizon and close. NOT COVERED: MuJoCo rigid-body dynamics, contacts, actuators, sensors, cameras and the reward; the upstream sensor suite also returns qvel (9), robot_base_pose, env_states, task_info, camera RGB/depth frames, TCP pose, object poses and action sensors, with a key set that can change between resets. The real sizes and the omissions are in fidelity.gaps. The card's mock_strategy.preferred upstream-sim was not used because the gate cannot install/import the clone and package code must not import it; only the package fake backend is declared and no sim backend was run. Only catalogue classes are used (cap.world.reset.v1, cap.world.step.v1, cap.world.seed.v1), so there are no catalogue requests. The gate's warnings: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the family bridge only records the seed for the next reset, no native call); G8.NO_UNIT x3 for the bridge-derived integer inputs ticks and seed twice; G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE, because GymEnv deliberately declares no action_space and therefore no sourced limit exists on an actuating capability, so the suite awards CL2 instead of CL3. No limit or action bound was invented. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package. gate.digest is the digest the check printed.
